The area of one loop of the polar curve $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta +\frac{\pi }{6})$ is given by the integral

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /18}^{5\pi /18}{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta +\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?
question.worked_solution:
The given polar curve is the polar rose with $3$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /18}^{5\pi /18}{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta +\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/09bc06001905956e32a4ff8cfff25a875a6933e19c365b2f9b159d8711a05048.png)

Therefore, the total area bounded by the polar curve is 

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}=3\cdot A=\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /18}^{5\pi /18}{sin}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$
